quotes.t: No one saves us but ourselves, No one can and no one may. We ourselves must walk the path Buddhas merely teach the way. By ourselves is evil done, By ourselves is pain endured, By ourselves we cease from wrong, By ourselves become we pure.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Dhammapada, Ch. 165, as translated in The Dharma, or The Religion of Enlightenment; An Exposition of Buddhism (1896) by Paul Carus; variants for some years have included "We ourselves must walk the path but Buddhas clearly show the way", but this is not yet located in any of the original publications of Carus.

quotes.t: Thousands of candles can be lighted from a single candle, and the life of the candle will not be shortened. Happiness never decreases by being shared.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, From The Teaching of Buddha, by Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (Society for the Promotion of Buddhism), Pg 132. It is a paraphrased version of Section 10 of the Sutra of Forty-two Sections

quotes.t: Let my skin and sinews and bones dry up, together with all the flesh and blood of my body! I welcome it! But I will not move from this spot until I have attained the supreme and final wisdom.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, The Jatka (From the Attainment of the Buddhaship. Also is in the Nirvana Sutta.)

quotes.t: Thousands of candles can be lit from a single candle, And the life of the candle will not be shortened. Happiness never decreases by being shared.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, From The Teaching of Buddha, by Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (Society for the Promotion of Buddhism), Pg 132. It is a paraphrased version of Section 10 of the Sutra of Forty-two Sections

quotes.t: ... all in any form, in any manner, and in any place, is unconditionally and once for all, prohibited for all. Thus, Mahāmati, meat-eating I have not permitted to anyone, I do not permit, I will not permit. Meat-eating, I tell you, Mahāmati, is not proper for homeless monks.
quotes.c: Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter Eight. On Meat-eating

quotes.t: After my nirvana, how will people who eat the flesh of beings deserve to be called disciples of Śākyamuni? You should understand that these people who eat flesh may gain some modicum of mental awakening while practicing samādhi, but they are all great rākṣasas who in the end must fall into the sea of death and rebirth. They are not disciples of the Buddha. Such people kill and devour each other, feeding on each other in an endless cycle. How could they possibly get out of the three realms? When you teach people in the world to practice samādhi, teach them to renounce all killing.
quotes.c: Śūraṅgama Sūtra, Part VII, Chapter 2: On Killing

quotes.t: All of you Bhikshus, after my Nirvana, you should revere and honor the Pratimoksha. It is like finding a light in darkness, or like a poor person obtaining a treasure. You should know that it is your great teacher, and is not different from my actual presence in the world.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: All of you Bhikshus, you should always singlemindedly and diligently seek the way out of all the moving and unmoving dharmas of the world, for they are all decaying, destructible, insecure appearances. All of you, stop; there is nothing more to say. Time is passing away, and I wish to cross over to Nirvana. These are my very last instructions.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: Any kind of material form whatever, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, all material form should be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: "This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self."
quotes.c: Majjhima Nikaya (Middle Length Discourses), Sutta 62, verse 3, p. 527

quotes.t: As rain breaks through an ill-thatched house, passion will break through an unreflecting mind.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Dhammapada, Ch. 1: The Twin Verses, verse 13

quotes.t: Behold now, Bhikkhus, I exhort you: All compounded things are subject to decay. Strive with diligence!
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Last words, as quoted in DN 16; Mahaparinibbana Sutta 6:8

quotes.t: Can there be joy and laughter When always the world is ablaze? Enshrouded in darkness Should you not seek a light? Can there be joy and laughter When always the world is ablaze? Enshrouded in darkness Should you not seek a light?
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Dhammapada

quotes.t: Conquer anger with love, evil with good, meanness with generosity, and lies with truth.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Dhammapada, Ch. 17, Verse 223

quotes.t: Develop the mind of equilibrium. You will always be getting praise and blame, but do not let either affect the poise of the mind: follow the calmness, the absence of pride.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Sutta Nipāta

quotes.t: Do not complain and cry and pray, but open your eyes and see, for the light is all about you, and it is so wonderful, so beautiful, so far beyond anything of which men have ever dreamt, for which they have ever prayed, and it is for ever and for ever.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Quoted by Charles Webster Leadbeater, in The Masters and the Path (1925) p. 229

quotes.t: Faith is the best wealth for a man in this world. Righteousness when well practised brings happiness. Truth is the sweetest of flavours. They say the life of one living by wisdom is the best.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta Nipata (Suttas falling down), § 182

quotes.t: For fear of causing terror to living beings, Mahāmati, let the Bodhisattva who is disciplining himself to attain compassion, refrain from eating flesh.
quotes.c: Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter Eight. On Meat-eating

quotes.t: From eating arrogance is born, from arrogance erroneous imaginations issue, and from imagination is born greed; and for this reason refrain from eating.
quotes.c: Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter Eight. On Meat-eating

quotes.t: He abused me, he struck me, he overcame me, he robbed me' -- in those who do not harbor such thoughts hatred will cease.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Dhammapada, 1.3-4; as translated by Radhakrishnan.

quotes.t: How then can it be compassionate to gorge on other beings' blood and flesh? Monks who will not wear silks from the East, whether coarse or fine; who will not wear shoes or boots of leather, nor furs, nor birds' down from our own country; and who will not consume milk, curds, or ghee, have truly freed themselves from the world.
quotes.c: Śūraṅgama Sūtra, Part VII, Chapter 2: On Killing

quotes.t: I can affirm that a person who neither eats the flesh of other beings nor wears any part of the bodies of other beings, nor even thinks of eating or wearing these things, is a person who will gain liberation.
quotes.c: Śūraṅgama Sūtra, Part VII, Chapter 2: On Killing

quotes.t: I spit on my life. Death in battle would be better for me than that I, defeated, survive.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta 3.2. Padhana Sutta, This statement is made in reference to his battle against the personification of temptation to evil, Mara.

quotes.t: I teach one thing and one only: suffering and the end of suffering.... Just as a mother would protect with her life her own son, her only son, so one should cultivate an unbounded mind towards all beings, and loving-kindness towards all the world. One should cultivate an unbounded mind, above and below and across, without obstruction, without enmity, without rivalry. Standing, or going, or seated, or lying down, as long as one is free from drowsiness, one should practice this mindfulness. This, they say, is the holy state here.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Sutta Nipata

quotes.t: I will go about, from kingdom to kingdom,:training many disciples.:They - heedful, resolute:doing my teachings -:despite your wishes, will go:where, having gone,:there's no grief.:* Sn 3.2, Buddha's Purpose
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta 3.2. Padhana Sutta

quotes.t: I will not take final Nirvana until I have nuns and female disciples who are accomplished... until I have laywomen followers...who will.... teach the Dhamma
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, as quoted by Dr Bettany Hughes Telegraph

quotes.t: If you have all sorts of idle discussions, your mind will be scattered, and even though you have left the home life, you will not attain liberation... you should quickly renounce and distance yourself from having a scattered mind and idle discussions. If you wish to be one who attains the bliss of still Extinction, you only need to be skillfully eliminate the peril of idle discussions.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: If you have doubt about suffering and the other Four Truths, you may quickly ask about them now. Do not harbor doubts and fail to clear them up.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: If you have wisdom, you will be without greed or attachment. Always examine yourselves, and do not allow yourselves to have faults, for it is in this way that you will be able to obtain liberation within my Dharma.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: If, Mahāmati, meat is not eaten by anybody for any reason, there will be no destroyer of life.
quotes.c: Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter Eight. On Meat-eating

quotes.t: In Aryans' Discipline, to build a friendship is to build wealth, to maintain a friendship is to maintain wealth and to end a friendship is to end wealth.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Cakkavatti Sutta, Patika Vagga, Digha Nikaya

quotes.t: In a world become blind, I beat the drum of the Deathless.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Ariyapariyesana Sutta

quotes.t: In all things, there is neither male nor female.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Vimalakriti Sutra, as quoted by Dr Bettany Hughes Telegraph

quotes.t: In what is seen, there should be just the seen; In what is heard, there should be just the heard; In what is sensed; there should be just the sensed; In what is thought, there should be just the thought.... He should not kill a living being, nor cause it to be killed, nor should he incite another to kill. Do not injure any being, either strong or weak in the world.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Sutta Nipāta II,14

quotes.t: Indeed, wisdom is born of meditation; without meditation wisdom is lost. Knowing this twofold path of gain and loss of wisdom, one should conduct oneself so that wisdom may increase.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Dhammapada, Ch. 20, Verse 282 Cut off your affection in the manner of a man who plucks with his hand an autumn lotus. Cultivate only the path to peace, Nirvana, as made known by the Exalted One. Ch. 20, Verse 285

quotes.t: Just as a bird, wherever it goes, flies with its wings as its only burden, so too, the bhikkhu becomes content with robes to protect his body and with almsfood to maintain his stomach, and wherever he goes he sets out taking only these with him. Possessing this aggregate of noble virtue, he experiences within himself a bliss that is blameless.
quotes.c: Majjhima Nikaya (Middle Length Discourses), Sutta 51, Verse 15, p. 450

quotes.t: Just as the eldest son of a wheel-turning monarch properly keeps in motion the wheel of sovereignty set in motion by his father, so do you, Sāriputta, properly keep in motion the Wheel of Dhamma set in motion by me.
quotes.c: Samyutta Nikaya (Connected Discourses), Vangisasamyutta, as translated by Bhikkhu Bodhi (2000), p. 287

quotes.t: Leaving behind son and wife, and father and mother, and wealth and grain, and relatives, and sensual pleasures to the limit, one should wander solitary as a rhinoceros horn.: 'This is an attachment; here there is little happiness, and little satisfaction; here there is very much misery; this is a hook.' Knowing this, a thoughtful man should wander solitary as a rhinoceros horn.: Having torn one's fetters asunder, like a fish breaking a net in the water, not returning, like a fire not going back to what is already burned, one should wander solitary as a rhinoceros horn.:* § 60-62
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta Nipata (Suttas falling down)

quotes.t: Let your love flow outward through the universe, To its height, its depth, its broad extent, A limitless love, without hatred or enmity. Then, as you stand or walk, Sit or lie down, As long as you are awake, Strive for this with a one-pointed mind; Your life will bring heaven to earth.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Passages of the Metta Sutta from the Sutta Nipata translated as "Discourse on Good Will" in the anthology God Makes the Rivers to Flow (1982; 2009), by Eknath Easwaran; also included in the anthology Timeless Wisdom (2008) by the same author.

quotes.t: Listen well, listen well, and mull it over in your thoughts!
quotes.c: Vimalakirti Sutra, To Ratnākara, on the practices carried out by bodhisattvas in purifying the lands. Chapter I, as translated by Burton Watson, Columbia University Press, 2000, ISBN: 0231106572.

quotes.t: Make an island of yourself, make yourself your refuge; there is no other refuge. Make truth your island, make truth your refuge; there is no other refuge.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Digha Nikaya, 16

quotes.t: Monks, a lay follower should not engage in five types of business. Which five? Business in weapons, business in human beings, business in meat, business in intoxicants, and business in poison.
quotes.c: Anguttara Nikaya (Numerical Discourses), 5.177: Vanijja Sutta, as translated by Thanissaro Bhikkhu (2001)

quotes.t: Not by birth does one become an outcaste, not by birth does one become a brahman. By one's action one becomes an outcaste, by one's action one becomes a brahman.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta Nipata (Suttas falling down), § 136

quotes.t: One day, Ananda, who had been thinking deeply about things for a while, turned to the Buddha and exclaimed: "Lord, I've been thinking - spiritual friendship is at least half of the spiritual life!" The Buddha replied: "Say not so, Ananda, say not so. Spiritual friendship is the whole of the spiritual life!"
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Gautama Buddha, Samyutta Nikaya, Mahāvagga, verse 2

quotes.t: One should follow a man of wisdom who rebukes one for one's faults, as one would follow a guide to some buried treasure. To one who follows such a wise man, it will be an advantage and not a disadvantage.... These teachings are like a raft, to be abandoned once you have crossed the flood. Since you should abandon even good states of mind generated by these teachings, how much more so should you abandon bad states of mind!... Conquer the angry man by love. Conquer the ill-natured man by goodness. Conquer the miser with generosity. Conquer the liar with truth.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Dhammapada

quotes.t: One with true wisdom is a secure boat for crossing over the ocean of old age, sickness, and death. He is also like a great bright lamp in the darkness of ignorance, a good medicine for all kinds of illnesses, and a sharp axe for cutting down the tree of afflictions.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: Rahula, develop meditation that is like water.... Just as people wash clean things and dirty things, excrement, urine, spittle, pus, and blood in water, and the water is not horrified, humiliated, and disgusted because of that, so too, Rahula, develop meditation that is like water.
quotes.c: Majjhima Nikaya (Middle Length Discourses), Sutta 62, verse 14, p. 530

quotes.t: Seclusion is happiness for the content one, one who sees the Dhamma that was heard; No ill-will is happiness in the world, restraint to living beings.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Gautama Buddha, Udāna

quotes.t: Sensual passions are your first enemy.:Your second is called Discontent.:Your third is Hunger & Thirst.:Your fourth is called Craving.:Fifth is Sloth & Drowsiness.:Sixth is called Terror.:Your seventh is Uncertainty.:Hypocrisy & Stubbornness, your eighth.:Gains, Offerings, Fame, & Status wrongly gained,:and whoever would praise self:& disparage others.:That, Namuci, is your enemy,:the Dark One's commando force.:A coward can't defeat it,:but one having defeated it:gains bliss.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta 3.2. Padhana Sutta

quotes.t: Shariputra, it is the failings of living beings that prevent them from seeing the marvelous purity of the land of the Buddha, the Thus Come One. The Thus Come One is not to blame. Shariputra, this land of mine is pure, but you fail to see it.
quotes.c: Vimalakirti Sutra, Chapter I, as translated by Burton Watson, Columbia University Press, 2000, ISBN: 0231106572. [detail.jpg|thumb|All of you Bhikshus, after my Nirvana, you should revere and honor the Pratimoksha. It is like finding a light in darkness, or like a poor person obtaining a treasure. You should know that it is your great teacher, and is not different from my actual presence in the world.]

quotes.t: That army of yours,:that the world with its devas can't overcome,:I will smash with discernment
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta 3.2. Padhana Sutta

quotes.t: That bhikkhu who has cut off passion in its entirety, like one picking a lotus, both flower and stalk, leaves this shore and the far shore as a snake leaves its old worn-out skin.: That bhikkhu who has cut off craving in its entirety, like one drying up a fast-flowing stream, leaves this shore and the far shore as a snake leaves its old worn-out skin.:* § 2-3
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta Nipata (Suttas falling down)

quotes.t: The Dharma for benefiting oneself and others is complete. If I were to live longer it would be of no further benefit. All of those who could be crossed over, whether in the heavens above or among humans, have already crossed over, and all of those who have not yet crossed over have already created the causes and conditions for crossing over. From now on all of my disciples must continuously practice. Then the Thus Come One' s Dharma body will always be present and indestructible.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: The brahman Kasibhāradvāja addressed the Blessed One with a verse.: 'You say you are a ploughman, but we do not see your ploughing. Being asked, tell us about your ploughing, so that we may know your ploughing.': 'Faith is the seed, penance is the rain, wisdom is my yoke and plough; modesty is the pole, mind is the yoke-tie, mindfulness is my ploughshare and goad....: Thus is this ploughing of mine ploughed. It has the death-free as its fruit. Having ploughed this ploughing one is freed from all misery.:* § 75-80
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta Nipata (Suttas falling down)

quotes.t: The food of the wise, Mahāmati, is what is eaten by the Rishis; it does not consist of meat and blood.
quotes.c: Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter Eight. On Meat-eating

quotes.t: The innumerable worlds in the cosmos are like the eyes of the net. Each and every world is different, its variety infinite. So too are the Dharma Doors (methods of cultivation) taught by the Buddhas.
quotes.c: Brahmajala Sutra, Sutra Translation Committee of the US and Canada (2000). The Brahma Net Sutra, New York Brahmajala Sutra (Mahayana)

quotes.t: The seers of old had fully restrained selves, and were austere. Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasures, they practiced their own welfare. The brahmans had no cattle, no gold, no wealth. They had study as their wealth and grain. They guarded the holy life as their treasure.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Sutta Nipata (Suttas falling down), § 284-285

quotes.t: The tongue is like a sharp knife, it kills without drawing blood; words in the hands of someone skilled can do more damage than a weapon in the hands of a warrior.
quotes.c: Digha Nikaya (Long Discourses), M. Walshe, trans. (1987), Sutta 1, verse 5

quotes.t: There are these four ways of answering questions. Which four? There are questions that should be answered categorically yes, no, this, that. There are questions that should be answered with an analytical (qualified) answer or redefining the terms. There are questions that should be answered with a counter-question. There are questions that should be put aside. These are the four ways of answering questions.
quotes.c: Pali Canon, Sutta Pitaka, As quoted in: Ṭhānissaro (Bhikkhu.) (2004) Handful of leaves. Vol. 3, p. 80

quotes.t: There is no meat to be regarded as pure in three ways: not premeditated, not asked for, and not impelled; therefore, refrain from eating meat.
quotes.c: Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter Eight. On Meat-eating

quotes.t: Things are not what they appear to be: nor are they otherwise.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Surangama Sutra

quotes.t: Through Knowledge (of Truth) All evils are washed away. The true Enlightened One stands firm, Scattering the clouds of delusion Like the sun shining in a cloudless sky.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Quoted in Jesus lived in India, p. 6

quotes.t: Thus, Mahāmati, wherever there is the evolution of living beings, let people cherish the thought of kinship with them, and, thinking that all beings are be loved as if they were an only child, let them refrain from eating meat. So with Bodhisattvas whose nature is compassion, eating of meat is to be avoided by him. Even in exceptional cases, it is not of a Bodhisattva of good standing to eat meat.
quotes.c: Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter Eight. On Meat-eating

quotes.t: To cease from evil, to do good, and to purify the mind yourself, this is the teaching of all the Buddhas.
quotes.c: Khuddaka Nikaya (Minor Collection), Dhammapada, Ch. 14, Verse 183

quotes.t: What is this world condition? Body is the world condition. And with body and form goes feeling, perception, consciousness, and all the activities throughout the world. The arising of form and the ceasing of form--everything that has been heard, sensed, and known, sought after and reached by the mind--all this is the embodied world, to be penetrated and realized.... The fool thinks he has won a battle when he bullies with harsh speech, but knowing how to be forbearing alone makes one victorious.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Samyutta Nikaya

quotes.t: Whatever an enemy might do to an enemy, or a foe to a foe, the ill-directed mind can do to you even worse. Whatever a mother, father or other kinsman might do for you, the well-directed mind can do for you even better.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Pali Canon 42-43 Cittavagga The Mind.

quotes.t: When the real nature of things becomes clear to the meditating Bikshu, then all his doubts fade away since he has learned what is that nature and what it's cause. From ignorance spring all the evils. From knowledge comes the cessation of this mass of misery, and then the meditating Brahmana stands dispelling the hosts of Mara like the sun that illuminates the sky.
quotes.c: Miscellaneous, Mahavagga 1st Khandhaka, as translated/quoted by Koot Hoomi, in The Mahatma Letters to A. P. Sinnett, Letter No. X, (1923), Letter No. X, 1881

quotes.t: When those in this assembly who have not yet done what should be done, see the Buddha cross over to Extinction, they will certainly feel sorrow. Those who have newly entered the Dharma and heard what the Buddha taught, will all cross over. They have seen the Way, like a flash of lightning in the night.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: Whereas some ascetics and Brahmins remain addicted to attending such shows as dancing, singing, music, displays, recitations, hand-music, cymbals and drums, fairy-shows, acrobatic and conjuring tricks, combats of elephants, buffaloes, bulls, goats, rams, cocks and quail, fighting with staves, boxing, wrestling, sham-fights, parades, manoeuvres and military reviews, the ascetic Gotama refrains from attending such displays.
quotes.c: Digha Nikaya (Long Discourses), M. Walshe, trans. (1987), Sutta 1, verse 1.13

quotes.t: You should increasingly benefit yourselves by acquiring hearing, contemplating, and cultivating wisdom. Even though a person only has flesh eyes, if he has illuminating wisdom, he has clear understanding.
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: You should know therefore, that everything in the world is impermanent. Meetings necessarily have separations, so do not harbor grief. Every appearance in the world is like this, so you should be vigorous and seek for an early liberation. Destroy the darkness of delusion with the brightness of wisdom. The world is truly dangerous and unstable, without any durability. My present attainment of Nirvana is like being rid of a malignant sickness. The body is a false name, drowning in the great ocean of birth, sickness, old age and death. How can one who is wise not be happy when he gets rid of it
quotes.c: The Bequeathed Teachings Sutra

quotes.t: Better than a thousand hollow words, is one word that brings peace.
All that we are is the result of what we have thought. The mind is everything. What we think, we become.
However many holy words you read, however many you speak, what good will they do you if you do not act on upon them?
Three things cannot be long hidden: the sun, the moon, and the truth.

I am not the first Buddha who came upon Earth, nor shall I be the last. In due time, another Buddha will arise in the world - a Holy One, a supremely enlightened One, endowed with wisdom in conduct, auspicious, knowing the universe, an incomparable leader of men, a master of angels and mortals.
Resolutely train yourself to attain peace.
Your worst enemy cannot harm you as much as your own unguarded thoughts.
'All conditioned things are impermanent' - when one sees this with wisdom, one turns away from suffering.
'As I am, so are these. As are these, so am I.' Drawing the parallel to yourself, neither kill nor get others to kill.
'As I am, so are they; as they are, so am I.' Comparing others with oneself, do not kill nor cause others to kill.
A disciplined mind brings happiness.
A mind unruffled by the vagaries of fortune, from sorrow freed, from defilements cleansed, from fear liberated - this is the greatest blessing.
A noble one produces an abundance of merit by having a compassionate mind towards all living beings.
A single lamp may light hundreds of thousands of lamps without itself being diminished.
A wise person should be urgently moved on occasions that make for urgency.
All experiences are preceded by mind, having mind as their master, created by mind.
All phenomena are preceded by the mind, created by the mind, and have the mind as their master.
All tremble at violence; all fear death. Putting oneself in the place of another, one should not kill nor cause another to kill.
Ardently do today what must be done. Who knows? Tomorrow, death comes.
As a water bead on a lotus leaf, as water on a red lily, does not adhere, so the sage does not adhere to the seen, the heard, or the sensed.
As an elephant in the battlefield withstands arrows shot from bows all around, even so shall I endure abuse.
Be a light unto yourself. Take refuge in yourself, and not in anything outside.
Better it is to live one day seeing the rise and fall of things than to live a hundred years without ever seeing the rise and fall of things.
Better than a thousand useless words is one useful word, upon hearing which one attains peace.
Both formerly and now, it is only suffering that I describe, and the cessation of suffering.
By oneself is evil done; by oneself is one defiled. By oneself is evil left undone; by oneself is one made pure.
Ceasing to do evil, Cultivating the good, Purifying the heart: This is the teaching of the Buddhas.
Conditions fall apart. Persist with diligence.
Conquer anger with non-anger. Conquer badness with goodness. Conquer meanness with generosity. Conquer dishonesty with truth.
Delight in heedfulness! Guard well your thoughts!
Do I speak at the right time, or not? Do I speak of facts, or not? Do I speak gently or harshly? Do I speak profitable words or not? Do I speak with a kindly heart, or inwardly malicious?
Do not scorn what you have received, nor envy the gains of others. He who envies others does not obtain peace of mind.
Don't sacrifice your own welfare for that of another, no matter how great. Realizing your own true welfare, be intent on just that.
Drop by drop is the water pot filled. Likewise, the wise man, gathering it little by little, fills himself with good.
Give, even if you only have a little.
Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased. This is a law eternal.
Hatred is never appeased by hatred. Hatred is appeased by love alone. This is an eternal law.

He who can curb his wrath as soon as it arises, as a timely antidote will check snake's venom that so quickly spreads, - such a monk gives up the here and the beyond, just as a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.
Heedfulness is the path to the Deathless. Heedlessness is the path to death. The heedful die not. The heedless are as if already dead.
I do not dispute with the world; rather it is the world that disputes with me.
I, too, do not envision a doctrine of self the clinging to which there would not arise sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
If a man going down into a river, swollen and swiftly flowing, is carried away by the current - how can he help others across? - The Buddha
If with a pure mind a person speaks or acts, happiness follows them like a never-departing shadow.
In the sky there are no tracks. Outside there is no recluse. There are no conditioned things that are eternal. There is no instability in the Buddhas.
Irrigators channel waters; fletchers straighten arrows; carpenters bend wood; the wise master themselves.
It is in the nature of things that joy arises in a person free from remorse.
It's a good thing to be satisfied with what one has.
